thread:
Jules (CSM): escalating on behalf of Neptune Analytics — they report that our rerank endpoint returns different scores for the same canonical input set after last night's rollout. customer claim: previously top doc had score ~0.92, now 0.67. they attached side-by-side JSON. they're pretty unhappy, asking for timeline and repro steps. :eyes:
support-bot: created ticket #INC-2026-1937 for Neptune Analytics — priority P1. auto-attached recent deploy logs.
deploy-bot: model-rollout v3.1 -> production by @ryan at 2025-11-02T03:14:12Z (variants: v3.1-fp16, v3.1-q8). Canary completed with 5% traffic, then full rollout.
Jules (CSM): tagging the oncall and model owners — @Isabel M and @Devon. customer pasted minimal repro, says results deterministic when calling our rerank endpoint with their prompt set.
Isabel M (ML Eng): thanks — can you paste the exact curl or SDK call you used? also need the model variant the tenant hit (we can route them).
Jules (CSM): pasted customer's sample call (redacted api key):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-v3","inputs":[{"query":"best ergonomic office chairs","candidates":["DocA","DocB","DocC"]}]}'
```
Customer said they ran this 10x and always get DocB > DocA now, whereas before DocA was top.
Devon (ML Eng): I pulled the exact input and replayed against our staging snapshots. Quick result:
```json
{"input_id":"n-a-123","scores_v3.0":[0.918,0.742,0.511],"scores_v3.1":[0.673,0.812,0.529]}
```
So scores flipped for DocA/DocB. reproduces locally with our model artifacts.
Isabel M (ML Eng): interesting. two immediate suspects: tokenizer change or numeric range shift from quantization. can you dump tokenization for the query and the candidates? also post the model commit hash and the serving config (quantize: true/false, kernel selection).
Devon (ML Eng): tokenization diff for the query "best ergonomic office chairs":
- v3.0 tokens: [101, 205, 809, 1011, 456] (len 5)
- v3.1 tokens: [101, 205, 809, 1011, 456, 0] (len 6)
candidate DocA token prefix also shows an extra leading token on v3.1. looks like a whitespace normalization change introduced in our tokenizer conversion script.
Isabel M (ML Eng): that would shift attention alignments and plausibly change rerank logits. did the commit also flip tokenizer versions? check deps.
Devon (ML Eng): model artifact metadata:
```
model: redwood/rerank-v3
commit: a1b2c3d4-2025-10-31
tokenizer: tokenlib v2.4 -> we accidentally packaged v2.5 in v3.1
serving: quantize=true (q8 path), kernel: auto-select
```
Ryan L (Infra): I can confirm deploy pipeline used the artifact with tokenlib v2.5; staging had v2.4. The pipeline step that rebuilds the tokenizer bundle had a changed flag - `--normalize-whitespace`. That was merged in the tokenizer bump PR.
Isabel M (ML Eng): OK that explains deterministic changes. quantization could amplify small tokenization shifts, but the root cause is tokenizer difference. two remediation paths: 1) patch the v3.1 artifact to use tokenlib v2.4 (rollback tokenizer bump) and re-deploy; 2) provide a compatibility shim that normalizes inputs to the v2.4 tokenization at serving time (faster but hacky). for customer SLA, quickest fix is to route Neptune to v3.0 until we ship a patched v3.1.
Jules (CSM): can we route them? customer wants a timeline and will require a temporary rollback if we can't guarantee no score regressions.
Ryan L (Infra): yes — I can add a per-tenant routing override to pin them to v3.0 for 24 hours. doing it now.
support-bot: routing override applied for tenant neptune-analytics -> model redwood/rerank-v3@v3.0, expires in 24h.
Devon (ML Eng): I ran a quick AB test with 500 samples from their eval set using v3.0 and v3.1; aggregated mean top-1 delta = -0.21 (worse for v3.1). attaching summary in ticket.
Isabel M (ML Eng): next steps for engineering: 1) create patch to re-run tokenizer build using v2.4, validate tokenization parity tests, 2) run full smoke eval on client's eval set to confirm parity, 3) decide whether to accept tokenlib change and retrain/rerank calibration or revert. I can own the parity test and calibration suggestions.
Devon (ML Eng): repro steps I used for internal validation (for the ticket):
1) checkout commit a1b2c3d4
2) pip install -r requirements.txt (ensure tokenlib==2.4 for baseline)
3) python -m rerank.replay --input sample_set.json --artifact ./artifacts/v3.1 --quantize true
4) compare scores with stored v3.0 snapshot using `jq` and a small python comparator.
Isabel M (ML Eng): also note that non-deterministic CPU kernel selection can introduce noise; we should pin kernels during the parity run: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=stable` in env.
Jules (CSM): I'll update the customer: explain root cause (tokenizer bump in packaging), temporary pin to v3.0, ETA for patch 6-12 hours, and offer to run their full eval set once we have patched build. anything to add?
Devon (ML Eng): include repro snippet and mention that scores are deterministic given artifact and tokenizer. add advice: they should avoid local canonicalization that differs from our prod pipeline.
Isabel M (ML Eng): once patch is ready I'll run the parity job and post the diff. if parity holds we can re-roll v3.1 with a migration note.
Jules (CSM): customer update sent. they asked for a postmortem when resolved. cc: @Ryan and @Isabel. :thumbsup:
Ryan L (Infra): I'll keep the routing override until the patch is validated. planning to start rollback plan if parity fails.
support-bot: ticket #INC-2026-1937 updated: routing override applied, engineering assigned, ETA 6-12h.
Jules (CSM): closing loop for now — will follow up in ticket and postmortem thread. thanks team. :heart:
